subject: physics
title: Non-flow processes and p-V diagrams
key_idea: A fixed amount of gas in a closed cylinder can change in four ways: isothermal, adiabatic, constant pressure and constant volume. The first law links each to heat, internal energy and work. The work done is the area under the curve on a p–V diagram.

sections.heading: The gas and the first law

blocks.text: A non-flow process keeps the same gas in a closed cylinder. This section covers the equation of state and the first law used on every process.

blocks.label: Equation of state of an ideal gas
where: R = molar gas constant, 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹

blocks.label: First law of thermodynamics
where: Q = heat transferred to the gas (J)
ΔU = increase in internal energy of the gas (J)
W = work done by the gas on its surroundings (J)

items: Heat **into** the gas makes Q positive. Heat out makes Q negative.
When the gas expands it does work, so W is positive. When it is compressed, W is negative.
The internal energy of an ideal gas is the kinetic energy of its molecules, so it depends only on temperature.
If the temperature is constant, ΔU = 0. If the temperature rises, ΔU is positive.
pV = nRT for a fixed amount of ideal gas.
Q = ΔU + W, with W the work done by the gas.
ΔU depends on the change in temperature only.

blocks.text: Each process fixes one thing. That fixed quantity decides what the first law reduces to.

items.meaning: A change at constant temperature. Heat flows in or out to keep T the same.
A change with no heat transfer to or from the surroundings, Q = 0. Usually it is fast, or the cylinder is insulated.
A change in which the pressure stays the same while volume and temperature change.
A change in which the gas cannot expand, so no work is done.

blocks.text: In pVᵞ = constant, γ is a constant for the gas. It is about 1.4 for air.

items: **Isothermal expansion:** the gas does work and takes in the same amount of heat. Temperature stays the same.
**Adiabatic expansion:** the gas does work using its own internal energy, so it **cools**.
**Adiabatic compression:** work done on the gas raises its internal energy, so it **warms**.
**Constant volume:** heat in only raises the temperature and pressure.

blocks.label: Work done at constant pressure
where: W = work done by the gas (J)

diagram.alt: A practice question. Work out the work done by a gas expanding at constant pressure, with new numbers each time.
diagram.question: A gas expands by {dV} dm³ at a constant pressure of {p} kPa. Calculate the work it does, in joules.

items: Isothermal: pV constant and ΔU = 0.
Adiabatic: pVᵞ constant and Q = 0.
Constant pressure: W = pΔV. Constant volume: W = 0.

blocks.text: A p–V diagram plots pressure against volume. The shape of each line shows the process, and the area gives the work.

items: Constant pressure is a **horizontal** line.
Constant volume is a **vertical** line, with no area under it, so W = 0.
An isothermal change is a curve of pV = constant.
An adiabatic change is a curve that falls more steeply than the isothermal through the same point.
The **area under the graph** is the work done by the gas.
When the gas expands the work done is positive. In a compression it is negative.
Estimate the area by counting squares or splitting it into shapes.
For a cycle that returns to its start, the work done per cycle is the **area of the loop**.

blocks.text: A loop traced clockwise is a net output of work. Expressions for work are only needed for the constant-pressure case, W = pΔV.

items: Work done is the area below the line on a p–V diagram.
Net work per cycle is the area enclosed by the loop.
Horizontal is constant pressure, vertical is constant volume.

checks.q: A gas at a constant pressure of 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa expands from 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Calculate the work done by the gas.
An ideal gas expands isothermally and takes in 250 J of heat. State the work done by the gas and explain your answer.
checks.a: 250 J. The temperature is constant, so ΔU = 0, and the first law Q = ΔU + W gives W = Q = 250 J.

checks.q: Explain why the temperature of a gas rises when it is compressed adiabatically.
checks.a: No heat is transferred, so Q = 0 and ΔU = −W. Work is done on the gas, so W is negative and ΔU is positive. The internal energy rises, so the temperature rises.
